bugs: A guest calling /api/posts without an `Accept: application/json` header gets a 500 error. The `auth` middleware redirects to route('login'), and the base app has no such route (routes/api.php:6, bootstrap/app.php unchanged).

Empty query filters (`?status=&tag=&per_page=`) return 422 instead of being ignored. The index rules have no `nullable`, and ConvertEmptyStringsToNull turns the empty values into nulls (app/Http/Requests/IndexPostRequest.php:14-16).
There is no PATCH route, so a partial update with PATCH returns 405 even though UpdatePostRequest uses `sometimes` rules meant for partial updates (routes/api.php:9).
antipatterns: routes/api.php:6-11 – four hand-written routes where `Route::apiResource('posts', ...)->except('show')` would cover them and also give PATCH
app/Observers/PostObserver.php:29 – the check-then-insert slug loop can race; the unique index is the only safeguard and a collision becomes a 500
app/Models/Post.php:55 – `firstOrCreate` for tags can race against the unique index; `createOrFirst` is safer
app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:36 – `->response()->setStatusCode(201)` is redundant; JsonResource already returns 201 for a model that was just created
strengths: Thin controller using `$request->user()->posts()`, `when()` with query scopes, `latest()->latest('id')` as a tie-breaker, and `withQueryString()`
Uses current Laravel attributes: #[Fillable], #[ObservedBy], #[Scope], and a `casts()` method with an enum cast
Ownership is checked with route-level `->can()`, so a non-author gets 403 before validation runs (and this is tested)
`$request->enum()` for the status filter is the idiomatic approach
syncTagNames uses a clean collection pipeline: trim, filter, uniqueStrict, then sync
Good tests: guards, slug uniqueness, reuse and de-duplication of tags, keeping an existing published_at, combined filters, pagination meta, and validation messages

bugs: No functional bugs found. As in impl-1, the slug check-then-insert loop can race under concurrent creates and turn into a 500 on the unique index (app/Observers/PostObserver.php:28).
antipatterns: routes/api.php:7-11 – separate PUT and PATCH route lines; `Route::apiResource('posts', ...)->except('show')->scoped(['post' => 'slug'])` would be more idiomatic
app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:20 – `PostStatus::from($request->validated('status'))` where `$request->enum('status', PostStatus::class)` is the idiomatic call
tests/Feature/PostApiTest.php:21 – `Http::preventStrayRequests()` is ceremony; the feature makes no HTTP calls
bootstrap/app.php – a `redirectGuestsTo` closure keyed on `is('api/*')` is a workaround; it is valid, but the path check duplicates what `shouldRenderJsonWhen` could express
strengths: Guests on the API get a JSON 401 even without an Accept header (handled in bootstrap/app.php and tested)
Route model binding by slug (`{post:slug}`) puts the generated slug to real use
PUT and PATCH are both supported, which suits the `sometimes` update rules
`createOrFirst` for tags is race-safe against the unique index
`nullable` index filters treat empty query parameters as absent (tested)
The policy's delete method reuses update, and the PostFactory defines a user_id default
Thorough tests: published_at kept across a draft→published round trip using `travel`, 403 before validation, `assertModelMissing`, empty filters, and a JSON 401 for a non-JSON guest request

v.rationale: The two implementations are nearly identical in structure. Both use an enum, an observer for the slug and published_at, route-level `->can()` with a policy, Form Requests, an API Resource, and modern attribute-based models. The ranking comes down to edge cases I confirmed with throwaway probe tests. impl-1 returns a 500 when a guest calls the API without an Accept: application/json header, because it redirects to a `login` route that doesn't exist. impl-1 also rejects empty query filters with 422 and has no PATCH route. impl-2 handles all three: it returns a JSON 401 for API guests, treats empty filters as absent using `nullable`, and routes PATCH. It also uses race-safe `createOrFirst` for tags and binds posts by slug. impl-1 is slightly more idiomatic in a couple of places: it uses `$request->enum` and `$request->integer`, and it avoids the needless `Http::preventStrayRequests`. Those are minor compared with impl-2's correctness advantages, so impl-2 ranks first.
